calls.reason: ARC Prize notes the tested o3 was trained on public ARC data, with no untrained comparison, and earlier MIT work scored 61.9% on a different split. But no slides were retrieved, so the misleading-graph charge can't be checked.

ARC Prize's April 22 report says released o3-high mostly failed to return outputs, answering 37 of 100 tasks. Those runs were left off the leaderboard, so the December 75.7% was not readily reproduced.

ARC Prize named o3-medium its strongest publicly available model, at 53% rather than the claimed 56%, against December's 75.7%. The gist holds; medium is a reasoning setting rather than a separate model.
The claim is hedged ('apparently'). It rests on Toby Ord's thread saying o3 searched for the puzzle answer, but the transcript screenshots needed to confirm this were not retrieved.
ARC Prize scores in spring 2025 were o3-low 41%, o3-medium 53% and o3-mini-high 35%, and o3-high runs were incomplete. No released o3 model came close to 75.7% in practice.
Expert grading of the March 2025 USAMO (Petrov et al.) found every model below 5% except Gemini-2.5-Pro at 24.4%. Testing began within hours of the problems' release.
